name: Duchy of Massa and Carrara
alt: Principality of Massa and Marquisate of Carrara

successors.name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
successors.text: the Duchy of Massa and the Principality of Carrara, 'annexed by her son and heir to the Duchy of Modena and Reggio' on Maria Beatrice's death in 1829

successors.name: Principality of Lucca and Piombino
successors.text: assigned to the Principality of Lucca and Piombino in 1806

successors.name: Cispadane Republic
successors.text: incorporated into the Cispadane Republic in 1796, which 'later became the Cisalpine Republic'

ledger.x: 22 February 1473: the Malaspina buy the Lordship of Carrara.
1520: Ricciarda Malaspina marries Lorenzo Cybo, and the Cybo-Malaspina line begins ('married in 1520 with Lorenzo Cybo'; in 1529 she obtained investiture of the marquisate from Charles V).
1568: Alberico I becomes Prince of Massa and Marquis of Carrara (ruler list: 'from 1568').
22 February 1664: the Principality of Massa becomes a duchy.
1796: the French take Massa and Carrara.
1806: Napoleon gives the duchy to Elisa's principality.
30 May 1814: French rule ends and the duchy returns to Maria Beatrice (infobox 'French rule: 10 May 1796-30 May 1814'; 'The Congress again assigned to Maria Beatrice the ancestral duchy').
1815: Maria Beatrice receives the Lunigiana fiefs.
December 1815: Francis IV takes the Lunigiana fiefs.

wars.name: French conquest of 1796
wars.outcome: 'In 1796 the Este were deprived of their possessions by the troops of Napoleon', who incorporated the land into the Cispadane Republic; French rule lasted from 10 May 1796 to 30 May 1814.

certainty.note: A small feudal state whose frontier with Lucca, Tuscany and Modena is not described on the pages; the French years 1796-1814 are not the duchy's.
Sharp from the Congress of Vienna settlement and the December 1815 transfer of the Lunigiana fiefs; the pages give no survey line, so the Lunigiana fiefs stay soft as a region.
